newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil eases on thin demand, Asia arb tempts.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil eases on thin demand, Asia arb tempts.

text.p: NWE gas oil cargo premiums were under pressure from low German end-user demand on Monday and interest blossomed in an arb to Asia built on soaring Chinese diesel demand, traders said.
A sharp $8 fall to $215.50 a tonne on Dec IPE futures and a move into Dec/Jan contango for the first time since August fuelled trader caution and slowed NEW business.

Futures slid on a slew of bearish news including the end of strikes at Elf refineries in France, talk of moderate weather in the United States and heaving buying on January by a European unit of a Wall Street trader.

Refinery grade heating oil cargo premiums were around unchanged at Dec IPE +$5/7 with low sulphur diesel premiums $2 lower at Dec IPE +$14/15 on increased capacity from a resumption of production at Elf refineries in France.
Refinery grade heating oil barge premiums were slightly firmer at Dec IPE -$0.50/0.00 but low sulphur diesel barge premiums in NWE were $1.50 softer at Dec IPE +$10/11.
A critical shortage of diesel in China has sent domestic prices above government ceilings and triggered extensive smuggling, industry sources in China said on Monday.
